<!-- 0.Data_pruning.Rmd — Prune species from the trait table and the tree and rebuild the exploration figures. -->
<!-- PhyloPhere | subworkflows/TRAIT_ANALYSIS/local/ -->

# Optional Data Pruning for Trait Analysis
This document describes the process of optionally pruning the dataset based on a user-provided list of species. 
This step ensures that only specified species are included in subsequent analyses.

Fast and easy.

## Setup and Directory Configuration

This section configures the working environment, sets directories, and loads necessary functions and libraries.

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# commons.R reads `params`, so it must be visible from the global environment.
if (!exists("params")) {
  stop("params object not found - ensure this Rmd is rendered with rmarkdown::render()")
}
tryCatch(assign("params", params, envir = .GlobalEnv), error = function(e) NULL)

# Call the setup function from commons.R
source("./src/commons.R")
setup_rmd()
source("./src/report_plots.R", local = TRUE)

# Fallback logger, used only when commons.R has not defined debug_log().
if (is.null(getOption("phylo_debug"))) {
  options(phylo_debug = TRUE)
}
if (!exists("phylo_debug_log", envir = .GlobalEnv)) {
  phylo_debug_log <- character()
}
if (!exists("debug_log", inherits = TRUE)) {
  debug_log <- function(...) {
    msg <- sprintf(...)
    phylo_debug_log <<- c(phylo_debug_log, msg)
    cat("[DEBUG] ", msg, "\n", sep = "")
  }
}

# ── Dependencies ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(reshape2)
library(ggrepel)
library(ggtree)
library(ggnewscale)
library(ggstar)
library(colorspace)
library(treeio)
library(tidytree)
library(phylolm)
library(ggtreeExtra)
library(geiger)
library(rphylopic)
library(paletteer)


# ── Labels, palettes and output directories ───────────────────────────────────

color_palette <- paste0(clade_name, "_palette") # name of the clade palette defined in palettes.R
capitalized_taxon <- tools::toTitleCase(taxon_of_interest)
capitalized_trait <- tools::toTitleCase(gsub("_", " ", trait)) # underscores shown as spaces
capitalized_clade <- tools::toTitleCase(gsub("_", " ", clade_name))

# Tableau 10 under colorblind-safe names.
tableau_10 <- paletteer_d("ggthemes::Tableau_10")
names(tableau_10) <- c(
  "blue", "orange", "vermillion", "bluish_green",
  "green", "yellow", "reddish_purple", "pink",
  "brown", "gray"
)

createDir(data_pruning_dir)

# Subdirectories of the pruning results.
extreme_plots_dir <- file.path(data_pruning_dir, "1.Extreme_plots")
asr_trees <- file.path(data_pruning_dir, "2.ASR_trees")
phylo_distribution_dir <- file.path(data_pruning_dir, "3.Phylo_distribution")

createDir(extreme_plots_dir)
createDir(asr_trees)
createDir(phylo_distribution_dir)

```
## Data Pruning Process
This section loads the prune list, prunes the trait data frame and phylogenetic tree, and saves the pruned data for downstream analyses.
```{r set_ourdirs, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

prune_list <- params$prune_list
prune_list_secondary <- params$prune_list_secondary

prune_log_msgs <- c()


# ── Prune lists ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# The primary prune list is required: one species per line.
if (prune_list != "") {
  prune_species_primary <- readLines(prune_list)
  prune_log_msgs <- c(prune_log_msgs, sprintf("Loaded prune list with %d species\n", length(prune_species_primary)))
} else {
  stop("No prune list provided. Please provide a valid list of species to prune.")
}

# Optional secondary prune list: species whose secondary trait value is blanked for the plots.
prune_species_secondary <- character(0)
if (prune_list_secondary != "") {
  prune_species_secondary <- readLines(prune_list_secondary)
  prune_log_msgs <- c(prune_log_msgs, sprintf("Loaded secondary prune list with %d species\n", length(prune_species_secondary)))
}


# ── Pruning ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Per-species statistics table (stats.f in stats.R).
stats_df <- stats.f(trait_df)

`%ni%` <- Negate(`%in%`)

# Species with NA in the primary trait, or in the n_trait/c_trait count columns when
# count data is used, are pruned together with the species of the prune list.
na_mask <- is.na(trait_df[[trait]])
if (isTRUE(has.n) && n_trait %in% names(trait_df)) {
  na_mask <- na_mask | is.na(trait_df[[n_trait]])
}
if (isTRUE(has.c) && c_trait %in% names(trait_df)) {
  na_mask <- na_mask | is.na(trait_df[[c_trait]])
}

prune_species_na <- trait_df$species[na_mask]
prune_species_na <- unique(prune_species_na[!is.na(prune_species_na)])

if (length(prune_species_na) > 0) {
  prune_log_msgs <- c(prune_log_msgs, sprintf("Identified %d species with NA phenotype/count values to prune\n", length(prune_species_na)))
}

# Union of the explicit prune list and the NA species.
all_prune_species <- unique(c(prune_species_primary, prune_species_na))

visualization_tree <- pruned_tree

pruned_trait_df <- trait_df[trait_df$species %ni% all_prune_species, ]
clean_tree <- ape::drop.tip(pruned_tree, intersect(pruned_tree$tip.label, all_prune_species))
pruned_stats <- stats.f(pruned_trait_df)

prune_log_msgs <- c(
  prune_log_msgs,
  sprintf("Pruned trait data frame has %d species\n", nrow(pruned_trait_df)),
  sprintf("Pruned tree has %d species\n", length(clean_tree$tip.label)),
  sprintf("Pruned stats data frame has %d species\n", nrow(pruned_stats))
)


# ── Pruned files ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# These are the files emitted for the following steps.
pruned_trait_file <- file.path(data_pruning_dir, "pruned_trait_file.tsv")
write.table(pruned_trait_df, file = pruned_trait_file, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
pruned_tree_file <- file.path(data_pruning_dir, "pruned_tree_file.nwk")
ape::write.tree(clean_tree, file = pruned_tree_file)
pruned_stats_file <- file.path(data_pruning_dir, "pruned_trait_stats.csv")
write.csv(pruned_stats, file = pruned_stats_file, row.names = FALSE)


# ── Plot data ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# The plots keep the pruned species but blank their trait values (NA), so the tree shows
# every species while the pruned ones carry no data. The emitted files above are unchanged.
nulled_trait_df <- trait_df
nulled_stats_df <- stats_df

if (length(prune_species_primary) > 0 && trait %in% names(nulled_trait_df)) {
  nulled_trait_df[nulled_trait_df$species %in% prune_species_primary, trait] <- NA
  nulled_stats_df[nulled_stats_df$species %in% prune_species_primary, trait] <- NA
  prune_log_msgs <- c(prune_log_msgs, sprintf("Nulled primary trait for %d species\n", sum(nulled_trait_df$species %in% prune_species_primary)))
}

if (length(prune_species_secondary) > 0 && nzchar(secondary_trait) && secondary_trait %in% names(nulled_trait_df)) {
  nulled_trait_df[nulled_trait_df$species %in% prune_species_secondary, secondary_trait] <- NA
  nulled_stats_df[nulled_stats_df$species %in% prune_species_secondary, secondary_trait] <- NA
  prune_log_msgs <- c(prune_log_msgs, sprintf("Nulled secondary trait for %d species\n", sum(nulled_trait_df$species %in% prune_species_secondary)))
}

cat(paste(prune_log_msgs, collapse = ""))

# From here on, trait_df and stats_df are the blanked versions used by the plots.
trait_df <- nulled_trait_df
stats_df <- nulled_stats_df

# Debug copies of the tables the plots use.
debug_log("Data pruning completed. Pruned trait file: %s, Pruned tree file: %s", pruned_trait_file, pruned_tree_file)
write.csv(stats_df, file = file.path(data_pruning_dir, "debug_pruned_stats.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(trait_df, file = file.path(data_pruning_dir, "debug_pruned_trait_df.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

```

# Rebuild figures

## 1. Load Melted Trait Data
This section loads pre-processed trait data in a long (melted) format and adds common names for species.

```{r, stat_visualization, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# ── Trait statistics ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

head(stats_df)

stats_df <- stats_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    value = .data[[trait]],
    taxa = .data[[taxon_of_interest]],
    common_name = gsub("_", " ", species)
  )

if(isTRUE(has.n)){
  stats_df <- stats_df %>%   
    mutate(N = .data[[n_trait]])
  debug_log("contrast_plot.f using n_trait = %s, missing N = %d", n_trait, sum(is.na(stats_df$N)))
}

# Species in tree order, so the plot rows follow the phylogeny.
ordered_species <-  tidytree::as_tibble(pruned_tree) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(.data$node)) %>%
  # Tip nodes are numbered 1..Ntip (ape convention). Filtering on `!is.na(label)` alone
  # would also admit internal-node support labels, which repeat across nodes and give
  # factor(levels =) duplicates.
  dplyr::filter(.data$node <= length(pruned_tree$tip.label)) %>%
  dplyr::pull(.data$label)

stats_df$species <- factor(stats_df$species, levels = ordered_species)
debug_log("contrast_plot.f ordered_species = %d", length(ordered_species))

# Taxa ordered by the first species of each taxon in tree order.
ordered_taxa <- ordered_species %>%
  sapply(function(sp) {
    idx <- which(stats_df$species == sp)
    if (length(idx) == 0) return(NA_character_)
    stats_df$taxa[idx[1]]
  }) %>%
  unname() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique()

stats_df <- stats_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(taxa = factor(taxa, levels = ordered_taxa)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(taxa, .by_group = TRUE)

```

# 3. Contrast Plots
This section generates contrast plots to visualize the trait across taxa, highlighting extreme values and outliers.

```{r phenoplot, fig.height=10, fig.width=15, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, dev='png', dpi=320}

# ── Contrast plot ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Trait values by taxon: one open circle per species, the global median as a dashed line
# and the per-taxon median as a bar. The foreground/background partition is not drawn
# here (4.Independent_contrasts.Rmd selects it). The sizes come from species_plot_profile().
# Implementation shared through src/report_plots.R.

plot_ready <- !is.null(stats_df) && nrow(stats_df) > 0
required_cols <- c("species", taxon_of_interest, trait)
plot_ready <- plot_ready && all(required_cols %in% names(stats_df))

if (!plot_ready) {
  message("Skipping contrast plot: missing or empty trait stats.")
} else {
  # get_palette_values() first, then a direct lookup of the clade palette as a fallback.
  palette_for_plot <- resolve_taxa_palette(stats_df$taxa, palette_name = color_palette)
  if (is.null(palette_for_plot) && exists("color_palette") && nzchar(color_palette)) {
    # Global environment, then the calling frame.
    if (exists(color_palette, envir = .GlobalEnv)) {
      palette_for_plot <- get(color_palette, envir = .GlobalEnv)
      debug_log("Retrieved palette '%s' directly from GlobalEnv: length = %d", color_palette, length(palette_for_plot))
    } else if (exists(color_palette, where = parent.frame(n = 1))) {
      palette_for_plot <- get(color_palette, pos = parent.frame(n = 1))
      debug_log("Retrieved palette '%s' from parent frame: length = %d", color_palette, length(palette_for_plot))
    }
  }
  debug_log("Calling contrast_plot.f with palette length: %d", ifelse(is.null(palette_for_plot), 0, length(palette_for_plot)))
  contrast_graph <- contrast_plot.f(stats_df, palette_for_plot, point_shape = 1)
  contrast_dims <- attr(contrast_graph, "plot_dims")
  knitr::opts_current$set(fig.width = contrast_dims$width, fig.height = contrast_dims$height)
  ggplot2::ggsave(
    file.path(extreme_plots_dir, paste0(trait, "_contrast_plot.png")),
    contrast_graph, device = "png", width = contrast_dims$width, height = contrast_dims$height, dpi = "retina"
  )
  contrast_graph
}

```

# 4. Violin Plots
This section generates violin plots to show trait distributions across taxa.

```{r violin_plot, fig.height=10, fig.width=8, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, dev='png', dpi=320}

# ── Violin plot ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Trait distribution by taxon: a violin per taxon, species as jittered points (outliers
# filled) and the global median as a vertical line.
# Implementation shared through src/report_plots.R.

if (!plot_ready) {
  message("Skipping violin plot: missing or empty trait stats.")
} else {
  violin_plot_path <- file.path(extreme_plots_dir, paste0(trait, "_violin_plot.png"))
  violin_graph <- violin_extremes.f(stats_df, trait, taxon_of_interest, point_shape = 1)
  violin_dims <- attr(violin_graph, "plot_dims")
  knitr::opts_current$set(fig.width = violin_dims$width, fig.height = violin_dims$height)
  ggplot2::ggsave(
    violin_plot_path,
    violin_graph, device = "png", width = violin_dims$width, height = violin_dims$height, dpi = "retina"
  )
  violin_graph
}
  
```

# 5. Ancestral State Reconstruction (ASR) Plots
This section generates ASR plots to visualize the evolutionary history of the trait across the phylogenetic
```{r asr_plot, fig.height=20, fig.width=17, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, dev='png', dpi=320}

# ── Ancestral state reconstruction ────────────────────────────────────────────

# Continuous ASR of the trait on the species tree. BM and OU are fitted with geiger and the
# OU model is kept when it improves AICc by at least 2 and alpha is above 1e-4. Node
# estimates and their 95% CI (ape::ace) are then used to flag tips that lie outside the CI
# of their immediate parent ("derived") or of all their ancestors ("cumulatively derived").
# Returns the node and tip tables, the model and a ggtree plot (element `plot`).
# Implementation shared through src/report_plots.R.

if (!plot_ready || nrow(stats_df) < 5) {
  plot.new()
  text(0.5, 0.5, "ASR plot skipped: at least five species required for BM/OU model comparison.", cex = 1.2)
} else {
  asr_plot_path <- file.path(asr_trees, paste0(trait, "_asr_tree.png"))
  asr_dims <- species_plot_profile(
    n_species = sum(!is.na(stats_df[[trait]]) & is.finite(stats_df[[trait]])),
    n_taxa = dplyr::n_distinct(stats_df[[taxon_of_interest]])
  )$asr
  knitr::opts_current$set(fig.width = asr_dims$width, fig.height = asr_dims$height)
  # One call renders and saves the plot, so the fit runs once. A failure is drawn as a
  # placeholder in the report, because message() is suppressed by message=FALSE and the
  # section would otherwise be empty with no visible reason.
  asr_result <- tryCatch(
    asr_tree.f(stats_df, pruned_tree, trait, taxon_of_interest),
    error = function(e) {
      plot.new()
      text(0.5, 0.5, paste("ASR plot failed:", conditionMessage(e)), cex = 1.1, col = "firebrick")
      NULL
    }
  )
  # asr_tree.f() returns a ggplot object, which is printed explicitly for the HTML output.
  # The PNG is written in both cases: the ggplot on success, a copy of the placeholder
  # device on failure, so the ASR_trees folder is never empty.
  if (!is.null(asr_result) && !is.null(asr_result$plot)) {
    print(asr_result$plot)
    tryCatch(
      ggplot2::ggsave(asr_plot_path, plot = asr_result$plot,
                       width = asr_dims$width, height = asr_dims$height,
                       dpi = 320, bg = "white", limitsize = FALSE),
      error = function(e) message("ASR plot file save failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
    )
  } else {
    tryCatch({
      grDevices::dev.copy(grDevices::png, filename = asr_plot_path,
                           width = asr_dims$width, height = asr_dims$height,
                           res = 320, bg = "white", units = "in")
      grDevices::dev.off()
    }, error = function(e) message("ASR plot file save failed: ", conditionMessage(e)))
  }
}

```

## 6. Fan Plot for Phylogenetic Distribution

This section creates a fan-shaped phylogenetic tree.

`r if (nrow(stats_df) < 3) "Fan tree skipped: at least three species are required." else ""`

```{r visual_distribution, eval=nrow(stats_df) >= 3, fig.height=15, fig.width=15, dev="png", dpi=320, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# ── Fan tree and trait rings ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

palette_values <- resolve_taxa_palette(stats_df$taxa, palette_name = color_palette)
# Fallback: the clade palette from the global environment.
if (is.null(palette_values) && exists("color_palette") && nzchar(color_palette)) {
  if (exists(color_palette, envir = .GlobalEnv)) {
    palette_values <- get(color_palette, envir = .GlobalEnv)
    debug_log("Retrieved palette '%s' directly from GlobalEnv for visual_distribution: length = %d", color_palette, length(palette_values))
  }
}
fill_scale <- if (is.null(palette_values)) {
  ggplot2::scale_fill_discrete()
} else {
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = palette_values)
}
color_scale <- if (is.null(palette_values)) {
  ggplot2::scale_color_discrete()
} else {
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = palette_values)
}

# Fan layout, saved as a bare tree first.
tree_profile_base <- species_plot_profile(
  n_species = length(visualization_tree$tip.label),
  n_taxa = dplyr::n_distinct(stats_df[[taxon_of_interest]]),
  n_rings = 0
)$tree
knitr::opts_current$set(fig.width = tree_profile_base$diagnostic_size, fig.height = tree_profile_base$diagnostic_size)
base_fan_tree <- ggtree(visualization_tree,
                        layout="fan",
                        open.angle=15, 
                        size=tree_profile_base$tree_line_width)

ggsave(file.path(phylo_distribution_dir, "big_tree.png"), base_fan_tree, device = "png", width = tree_profile_base$diagnostic_size, height = tree_profile_base$diagnostic_size, dpi = "retina")

ordered_species <- rev(visualization_tree$tip.label)
row.names(stats_df) <- stats_df$species

# Use the non-user-pruned tree copy for visualization so nulled species remain as tips.
tree_plot_trait_df <- stats_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(species %in% visualization_tree$tip.label)

circular_tree <- visualization_tree
debug_log("visual_distribution: circular_tree tips retained for visualization = %d", length(circular_tree$tip.label))

n_tips <- length(circular_tree$tip.label)
n_taxa_tree <- dplyr::n_distinct(tree_plot_trait_df$taxa)
n_fruit_rings <- if (isTRUE(has.secondary)) 2L else 1L
tree_profile <- species_plot_profile(n_species = n_tips, n_taxa = n_taxa_tree, n_rings = n_fruit_rings)$tree
tree_profile$n_label_nudge <- tree_profile$n_label_nudge + 0.45
tree_profile$asterisk_nudge <- tree_profile$asterisk_nudge + 0.10
tree_profile$asterisk_y <- tree_profile$asterisk_y + 0.04
trait_axis_nbreak <- as.integer(max(1, round(tree_profile$axis_nbreak)))
trait_axis_text_size <- as.numeric(tree_profile$axis_text_size)
secondary_axis_text_size <- as.numeric(tree_profile$axis_text_size * 0.8)
knitr::opts_current$set(fig.width = tree_profile$width, fig.height = tree_profile$height)

# One row per species with the summed trait (and N, p or secondary trait when present);
# species without a value are drawn with zero height and an asterisk.
tree_trait_data <- tree_plot_trait_df %>%
  group_by(species, taxa)

# Branch color trait: its ancestral states come from branch_trait_node_values()
# (plotting_fun.R), which tolerates duplicated species rows and partial coverage. When it
# returns NULL the branches are drawn plain.
branch_provenance <- NULL
if (isTRUE(has.branch)) {
  branch_provenance <- branch_cache_provenance(
    circular_tree, tree_trait_data$species, tree_trait_data[[branch_trait]], branch_trait)
  combined_br_data <- read_branch_cache(params$branch_node_values_file, branch_provenance)
  if (is.null(combined_br_data)) {
    combined_br_data <- branch_trait_node_values(
      circular_tree, tree_trait_data$species, tree_trait_data[[branch_trait]])
  }
  if (is.null(combined_br_data)) has.branch <- FALSE
}
  
if (isTRUE(has.n) && isTRUE(has.secondary)) { # N and secondary trait
  tree_trait_data <- tree_trait_data %>%
    dplyr::rename(secondary_value = .data[[secondary_trait]]) %>%
    summarize(
      trait_sum = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE),
      trait_is_na = all(is.na(value)),
      n_sum = sum(N, na.rm = TRUE),
      secondary_sum = sum(secondary_value, na.rm = TRUE),
      secondary_is_na = all(is.na(secondary_value)),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
} else if (isTRUE(has.n)) {
  tree_trait_data <- tree_trait_data %>%
    summarize(
      trait_sum = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE),
      trait_is_na = all(is.na(value)),
      n_sum = sum(N, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop") %>%
    ungroup()
} else if (isTRUE(has.secondary)) { # secondary trait only
  tree_trait_data <- tree_trait_data %>%
    dplyr::rename(secondary_value = .data[[secondary_trait]]) %>%
    summarize(
      trait_sum = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE),
      trait_is_na = all(is.na(value)),
      secondary_sum = sum(secondary_value, na.rm = TRUE),
      secondary_is_na = all(is.na(secondary_value)),
      .groups = "drop") %>%
    ungroup()
} else { # neither N nor secondary trait
  tree_trait_data <- tree_trait_data %>%
    summarize(
      trait_sum = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE),
      trait_is_na = all(is.na(value)),
      .groups = "drop") %>%
    ungroup()
}

tree_trait_data <- tree_trait_data %>%
  mutate(
    trait_sum_plot = ifelse(trait_is_na, 0, trait_sum),
    trait_fill = ifelse(trait_is_na, 0, trait_sum),
    trait_asterisk = ifelse(trait_is_na, "*", "")
  )

if (isTRUE(has.secondary)) {
  tree_trait_data <- tree_trait_data %>%
    mutate(
      secondary_sum_plot = ifelse(secondary_is_na, 0, secondary_sum),
      secondary_fill = ifelse(secondary_is_na, 0, secondary_sum),
      secondary_asterisk = ifelse(secondary_is_na, "*", "")
    )
}

primary_ring_limits <- compute_ring_axis_limits(tree_trait_data$trait_sum_plot, min_limit = 1)
secondary_ring_limits <- if (isTRUE(has.secondary)) compute_ring_axis_limits(tree_trait_data$secondary_sum_plot, min_limit = 1) else c(0, 1)

# Tree as a tibble joined with the trait data.
tree_tibble <- tidytree::as_tibble(circular_tree) %>%
  dplyr::rename(species = label)

tree_with_traits <- full_join(tree_tibble, tree_trait_data, by = 'species')

# Node values of the branch trait.
if (isTRUE(has.branch)) {
  tree_with_traits <- full_join(tree_with_traits, combined_br_data, by = 'node')
}

# Debug export of the joined table.
write.csv(tree_with_traits, file.path(phylo_distribution_dir, "tree_with_traits.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
if (isTRUE(has.branch)) {
  saveRDS(branch_provenance,
          paste0(file.path(phylo_distribution_dir, "tree_with_traits.csv"), ".branch_cache.rds"))
}

# treedata object for ggtree.
tree_data_object <- tidytree::as.treedata(tree_with_traits)

# Diagnostic tree with node numbers, colored by taxon.
diagnostic_tree <- ggtree(tree_data_object,
                          layout = "fan",
                          open.angle = 15,
                          size = tree_profile$tree_line_width) +
  geom_text2(aes(label = node), hjust = -0.5, vjust = -0.5, size = tree_profile$node_text_size) +
  aes(color = taxa) +
  color_scale

ggsave(file.path(phylo_distribution_dir, "diagnostic_tree.png"), diagnostic_tree, device = "png", width = tree_profile$diagnostic_size, height = tree_profile$diagnostic_size, dpi = "retina")

# Base tree, with the branch trait (column BR) as a color gradient when present.
if (isTRUE(has.branch)) {
  capitalized_branch_trait <- tools::toTitleCase(gsub("_", " ", branch_trait))
  tree_plot_step1 <- ggtree(tree_data_object, aes(color = BR),
                                  layout="fan",
                                  open.angle=15, 
                                  size=tree_profile$tree_line_width) +
    scale_color_gradient(
      name = capitalized_branch_trait,
      low = "#F4EBD0", high = "#2B2D42",
      # Branches that subtend too few covered species have no reconstruction and are grey.
      na.value = "grey70",
                        guide = guide_colorbar(order = 3)) +  # legend order: branch trait last
    new_scale_color()
} else {
  tree_plot_step1 <- ggtree(tree_data_object,
                                  layout="fan",
                                  open.angle=15, 
                                  size=tree_profile$tree_line_width)
}  

  tree_plot_step1 <- tree_plot_step1 +
  # Ring of trait bars
  geom_fruit(
    geom = geom_col,
    mapping = aes(y = species, x = trait_sum_plot, fill = trait_fill, width = 0.5),
    alpha = 0.5,
    show.legend = TRUE,
    pwidth = tree_profile$fruit_pwidth,
    color = "black",
    size = 0.7,
    axis.params = list(
      axis = 'x',
      text.size = trait_axis_text_size,
      nbreak = trait_axis_nbreak,
      text.angle = 270,
      vjust = 0.5,
      hjust = 0,
      limits = primary_ring_limits
    ),
    grid.params = list()
    ) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    name = capitalized_trait, 
    low = "white", 
    high = tableau_10["blue"],
    guide = guide_colorbar(order = 1),
    aesthetics = "fill"
  ) +
  new_scale_fill()

# Second ring for the secondary trait.
if (isTRUE(has.secondary)) {
  capitalized_secondary_trait <- tools::toTitleCase(gsub("_", " ", secondary_trait))

  tree_plot_step1 <- tree_plot_step1 +
    geom_fruit(
      geom = geom_col,
      offset = -tree_profile$fruit_pwidth,
      mapping = aes(y = species, x = secondary_sum_plot, fill = secondary_fill, width = 0.5),
      alpha = 0.5,
      show.legend = TRUE,
      pwidth = tree_profile$fruit_pwidth,
      color = "black",
      size = 0.7,
      axis.params = list(
        axis = 'x',
        text.size = 0,
        nbreak = 0,
        text.angle = 270,
        vjust = 0.5,
        hjust = 0,
        limits = secondary_ring_limits
      ),
      grid.params = list()
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(
      name = capitalized_secondary_trait, 
      low = "white", 
      high = tableau_10["vermillion"],
      guide = guide_colorbar(order = 2),
      aesthetics = "fill"
    ) +
    new_scale_fill()
}

# geom_fruit sizes the trait rings to `fruit_pwidth` and scales the bars against
# `axis.params$limits`, but a bar can still extend past that band (an outlier value, the
# axis tick labels), depending on where the data sit relative to the limits. Instead of a
# fixed margin, the end of the ring stack is measured with fan_label_offsets() (as for the
# label ring), and only the part not covered by the nominal offset of the taxa ring is added.
trait_ring_measure <- fan_label_offsets(tree_plot_step1, labels = character(), ring_gap = 0, image_gap = 0)
trait_ring_span_fraction <- if (trait_ring_measure$tip_radius > 0) {
  (trait_ring_measure$outer_radius - trait_ring_measure$tip_radius) / trait_ring_measure$tip_radius
} else {
  tree_profile$fruit_pwidth
}
taxa_bar_offset_effective <- tree_profile$taxa_bar_offset +
  max(0, trait_ring_span_fraction - tree_profile$fruit_pwidth)

# Ring that marks the taxon of each species.
tree_plot_step2 <- tree_plot_step1 +
  geom_fruit(geom = geom_col,
             mapping = aes(y = species, x = 1, fill = taxa),
             pwidth = tree_profile$taxa_bar_pwidth, color = "black", linewidth = 0.5, offset = taxa_bar_offset_effective)

if (!is.null(palette_values) && length(palette_values) > 0) {
  tree_plot_step2 <- tree_plot_step2 + scale_fill_manual(values = palette_values, breaks = 0)
}

tree_plot_step2 <- tree_plot_step2 +
  new_scale_fill() +
  theme_tree() +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),  
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),
        legend.position = "none",
        plot.title = element_text(size = 17, margin = margin(t = 0, r = 0, b = -1.25, l = 0, unit = "cm")),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 15, margin = margin(t = 0, r = 0, b = -1.5, l = 0, unit = "cm"))
  )

# Sample size (N) labels, when available.
if(isTRUE(has.n)){
  tree_plot_step3 <- tree_plot_step2 +
    geom_text(aes(label = n_sum), nudge_x = tree_profile$n_label_nudge, fontface = "bold", size = tree_profile$n_label_size, vjust = 0.5)
} else {
  tree_plot_step3 <- tree_plot_step2
}

# Asterisks mark species whose trait value is missing (blanked or absent).
tree_plot_step3 <- tree_plot_step3 +
  geom_text(aes(label = trait_asterisk),
            nudge_x = tree_profile$asterisk_nudge, nudge_y = tree_profile$asterisk_y,
            color = tableau_10["blue"],
            fontface = "bold",
            size = tree_profile$asterisk_size,
            vjust = 0.5)

if (isTRUE(has.secondary)) {
  tree_plot_step3 <- tree_plot_step3 +
    geom_text(aes(label = secondary_asterisk),
              nudge_x = tree_profile$asterisk_nudge, nudge_y = -tree_profile$asterisk_y,
              color = tableau_10["vermillion"],
              fontface = "bold",
              size = tree_profile$asterisk_size,
              vjust = 0.5)
}

dyn_height <- tree_profile$height
dyn_width <- tree_profile$width

```
```{r visual_distribution_final, eval=nrow(stats_df) >= 3, fig.height=if (nrow(stats_df) >= 3) dyn_height else 10, fig.width=if (nrow(stats_df) >= 3) dyn_width else 10, dev="png", dpi=320, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# ── Taxon labels and silhouettes ──────────────────────────────────────────────

# Most recent common ancestor node of each taxon.
tip_df <- find_taxon_mrca(circular_tree, tree_with_traits)

# One phylopic silhouette (rphylopic UUID) per taxon name.
tip_df <- tip_df %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(phylopic_UUID = rphylopic::get_uuid(name = taxa, n = 1))

# Debug export.
write.csv(tip_df, file.path(phylo_distribution_dir, "taxon_node_mapping.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# The label rings are placed relative to where the fruit rings end (see plotting_fun.R).
label_offsets <- fan_label_offsets(
  tree_plot_step3,
  labels = tip_df$taxa,
  label_fontsize = tree_profile$branch_label_size,
  canvas_in = dyn_height,
  ring_gap = tree_profile$label_ring_gap,
  image_gap = tree_profile$label_image_gap,
  image_size = tree_profile$image_size
)

# Silhouettes at the MRCA of each taxon, then the taxon names.
final_tree_plot <- tree_plot_step3 +
  geom_cladelab(data = tip_df,
                mapping = aes(
                  node = mrca_node,
                  label = taxa,
                  image = phylopic_UUID,
                  color = taxa),
                geom="phylopic",
                barsize = NA,
                offset = label_offsets$phylopic,
                imagesize = tree_profile$image_size,
                alpha = 0.75)

if (!is.null(palette_values) && length(palette_values) > 0) {
  final_tree_plot <- final_tree_plot + scale_color_manual(values = palette_values, breaks = 0)
}

final_tree_plot <- final_tree_plot +
  geom_cladelab(data = tip_df,
                mapping = aes(
                  node = mrca_node,
                  label = taxa),
                show.legend = FALSE,
                          color = "black",
                angle = "auto",
                horizontal = TRUE,
                offset = label_offsets$text,
                barsize = NA,
                fontsize = tree_profile$branch_label_size,
                fontface = "bold") +
  theme_tree() +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),  
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),
        legend.position = "right",
        # Key size and spacing are absolute lengths, so they scale with the canvas
        # together with the legend text.
        legend.spacing.y = unit(tree_profile$legend_spacing_cm, 'cm'),
        legend.title = element_text(
          size = tree_profile$legend_title_size, face = "bold",
          margin = margin(b = 15)),
        legend.key.size = unit(tree_profile$legend_key_cm, 'cm'),
        legend.text = element_text(size = tree_profile$legend_text_size),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 17, margin = margin(t = 0, r = 0, b = -1.25, l = 0, unit = "cm")),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 15, margin = margin(t = 0, r = 0, b = -1.5, l = 0, unit = "cm"))
  ) +
  # Caption for the asterisks.
  labs(caption = "\"*\" indicates that species was removed for this trait as part of the data pruning process\n(following color conventions)") +
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(size = tree_profile$caption_size, hjust = 0, face = "italic", margin = margin(b = 10)))

final_tree_plot

# One PNG per construction step of the tree.
ggsave(file.path(phylo_distribution_dir, "tree_with_trait_bars.png"), tree_plot_step1, device = "png", width = dyn_width, height = dyn_height, dpi = "retina")
ggsave(file.path(phylo_distribution_dir, "tree_with_taxa_bars.png"), tree_plot_step2, device = "png", width = dyn_width, height = dyn_height, dpi = "retina")
if(isTRUE(has.n)){
  ggsave(file.path(phylo_distribution_dir, "tree_with_n_labels.png"), tree_plot_step3, device = "png", width = dyn_width, height = dyn_height, dpi = "retina")
}
ggsave(file.path(phylo_distribution_dir, "final_tree_plot.png"), final_tree_plot, device = "png", width = dyn_width, height = dyn_height, dpi = "retina")
